faq.title: Questions before you begin
faq.imageAlt: A training room set up for a workshop

q1.a: Program A, Tourism Service Professional, is a two-level hybrid route with trainer-led sessions, a practical assignment and a demonstration certificate. Program B, Visitor Service Essentials, is one self-paced stage of short lessons and practice that measures your improvement, without a certificate. Program C, Destination Storytelling, is an illustrative sample of a possible future offering.

q2.q: What is the difference between self-paced and live learning?
q2.a: Self-paced units are videos, interactive modules and resources you complete whenever suits you, and you can resume where you stopped. Live learning happens in scheduled trainer sessions, in person or online, shown with the date and Qatar time. Program A includes one required session; Program B sessions are optional clinics.

q3.a: Program A issues a watermarked demonstration certificate once every requirement is met: assessments, attendance and a session score, and the practical assignment. It is a training completion record, not a guide licence. Program B and the Program C sample do not issue certificates.

q4.q: How do I access my account?
q4.a: Create an account with your email and a password, confirm your email through the demo verification step, then complete a short profile. Trainers and Academy administrators use accounts provided by the Academy. Choosing the trainer or admin sign-in mode never grants those roles.

q5.a: Each portal page explains what to do next, and every session lists its trainer and location. In this demonstration, Help requests go to the Academy team running the walkthrough.

A.title: Tourism Service Professional
A.audience: Service professionals who want a structured, certified route.
A.summary: Build service skills through self-paced learning, guided practice and trainer-led sessions. Complete assessments and a practical assignment to earn a demonstration certificate.
A.formatLine: Two levels • Hybrid • Approximately 4 hours • Certification track
A.heroAlt: A family walking at the National Museum of Qatar
A.prerequisites: A learner account and a completed profile. Level 2 sessions open once Level 1 is complete.
A.effort: Approximately 4 hours across two levels, including one 60-minute trainer-led session.
A.audienceDetail: Hotel, tour, transport, travel trade and venue professionals who want a structured route with trainer feedback.
A.outcome1: Welcome every visitor with a confident greeting, a useful question and a clear next step.
A.outcome2: Communicate clearly and inclusively, and check that the visitor has understood.
A.outcome3: Recover a difficult service moment with acknowledgement, feasible options and escalation.
A.outcome4: Apply your skills in a scored, trainer-led session in person or live online.
A.outcome5: Plan a helpful response to a changed booking in a practical assignment.

B.title: Visitor Service Essentials
B.audience: Anyone who serves visitors and wants a personalised starting point.
B.summary: Develop everyday visitor-service skills through a personalised selection of short lessons and realistic practice. Measure your improvement from start to finish.
B.formatLine: One stage • Self-paced • Approximately 60–90 minutes • No certificate
B.heroAlt: A family on a dhow with the Museum of Islamic Art behind them
B.prerequisites: None. Create an account and complete your profile. The pre-assessment shows where to start and is not an entry barrier.
B.effort: Approximately 60–90 minutes, self-paced, in one stage: Visitor Service Essentials.
B.audienceDetail: Anyone who serves visitors, whatever their role or organisation. Your profile shapes the selection and order of units.
B.outcome1: Find out what a visitor needs by asking about interests and available time.
B.outcome2: Explain options in plain language and check understanding.
B.outcome3: Respond to a disappointed visitor with care and realistic choices.
B.outcome4: Measure your improvement from your baseline to your post-assessment.

C.title: Destination Storytelling
C.audience: Illustrative sample of a possible future Academy offering.
C.summary: Explore a sample future Academy offering focused on clear, engaging destination stories.
C.formatLine: Additional sample programme • Overview and reporting preview
C.heroAlt: Visitors in the Qatar National Library
C.prerequisites: None. This is a sample overview for illustration only.
C.effort: A 5-minute preview with a fictional story-planning worksheet.
C.audienceDetail: Shown to illustrate how a future Academy offering could appear. It is not an actual Qatar Tourism programme.
C.outcome1: Plan a short destination story with a clear opening, one memorable detail and a close.
C.outcome2: Choose details you can verify and that suit the visitor in front of you.
C.outcome3: Tell the story in about five minutes using a fictional story-planning worksheet.

rules.a1Activity: Programme enrolment, profile and five-question baseline.
rules.a2Activity: Visitor welcome, clear communication, service recovery, an interactive branching scenario and a formative quiz.
rules.a2Outcome: Required units complete and foundation quiz at least {{n}} percent.
rules.a3Activity: Text or voice scenario with feedback and retry.
rules.a3Outcome: One attempt completed; the score is advisory.
rules.a4Activity: Choose an eligible in-person or live-online session, RSVP and attend.
rules.a4Outcome: Attendance marked and session score at least {{n}} percent.
rules.a5Activity: A visitor-service response plan or a short role-play recording, marked with a rubric.
rules.a5Outcome: Assignment at least {{n}} percent; revisions permitted.
rules.a6Activity: Parallel post-assessment with a competency comparison.
rules.a6Outcome: At least {{n}} percent; targeted review and retry available.
rules.a7Activity: The system checks every required condition before issuing.
rules.a7Outcome: Watermarked demonstration certificate and a verifiable certificate record.
rules.b1: Complete all core units in your learning path.
rules.b2: Complete one role-play, in text or voice mode.
rules.b3: Have your short visitor response approved.
rules.bNote: No minimum post score blocks completion. Below {{n}} percent we suggest a review. Practice scores are tracked separately from knowledge assessment scores. Program B issues no certificate, including after excellent scores. These are illustrative settings an administrator can edit.
rules.c: Sample overview only: viewing the preview completes it. Seeded reporting shows how a third programme would appear to administrators. There is no certificate.

scenario.title: Changed booking
scenario.opening: I booked this experience for today and now I am told it is unavailable. What can you do?
scenario.followUp: We only have the afternoon free, and there are four of us.

data.video: A helpful welcome begins with attention. Greet the visitor, introduce yourself and ask what they need today. Listen before suggesting an option. If the request is unclear, ask one short follow-up question. Offer information you can verify and explain the next step in plain language. Before the conversation ends, check that the visitor knows what to do next. A confident service experience is built through clarity, respect and follow-through.
